title: Cardamom Poached Pears
subtitle: Pears in a fragrant vanilla and cardamom syrup, served warm or cold
excerpt: Firm pears poached in a fragrant sugar syrup scented with cardamom, vanilla, and lemon until tender and glossy, with the syrup reduced and poured over to serve.
sourceNotes: A lighter, white-syrup alternative to the red wine version, allowing the pear flavour and the cardamom perfume to be the main notes. Cardamom with pear is a Scandinavian combination absorbed into British cooking through the pastry and restaurant trades.

recipe.makeAheadNotes: Best made 2 to 4 hours ahead. The pears absorb the cardamom further as they cool in the syrup.

content.text: Cardamom poached pears are cooked in a clear sugar syrup, keeping the pale gold colour of the fruit and letting the aromatic spice speak clearly. The syrup is lightly perfumed with cardamom pods, a vanilla pod, and lemon; it reduces to a thin, fragrant glaze after the pears come out. Serve warm or at room temperature, with crème fraîche or Greek yoghurt alongside.

items.prepNote: peel stripped in wide strips, plus the juice

content.text: Combine the water, sugar, cardamom pods, vanilla pod, and lemon peel and juice in a saucepan wide enough to hold the pears upright. Heat over a medium heat, stirring until the sugar has dissolved. Bring to a gentle simmer and cook for 5 minutes to let the flavours develop.

Peel the pears, leaving the stalks. Remove the core from the base of each with a melon baller or teaspoon. Lower the pears into the simmering syrup, standing them upright. Place a circle of baking paper directly on the surface. Cover and simmer over a low heat for 25 to 35 minutes, turning the pears gently halfway through, until a skewer meets no resistance through the thickest part.

Transfer the pears to a shallow dish. Strain the syrup back into the pan, discarding the solids. Boil over a high heat for 6 to 8 minutes until slightly thickened and reduced by about a third. Pour the warm syrup over the pears. Allow to cool for at least 30 minutes before serving, turning the pears in the syrup a couple of times.

items.symptom: The pears taste of very little after cooking
items.cause: Not enough cardamom, or the spices were old and had lost their volatiles.
items.fix: Use freshly purchased cardamom pods and crush them before adding. Increase to 10 pods if the cardamom is from an older batch.

items.symptom: The syrup is watery rather than glossy
items.fix: Continue reducing at a brisk simmer. The syrup should just barely coat a spoon and will thicken further as it cools.

items.symptom: The pears turned brown before adding to the syrup
items.cause: Exposed to air too long after peeling.
items.fix: Peel the pears directly into the warm syrup, or keep them in a bowl of water with a squeeze of lemon juice while you finish peeling the others.

content.text: Keeps in the fridge, covered in the syrup, for up to 3 days. Serve cold or at room temperature, the cardamom is more pronounced when not chilled. Do not freeze.
